Les_Paul, some eur/gbp charts for you.

The weekly up first for some top down viewing pleasure. The lower white line is support and resistance and its proven over time and miles back from price at present and was the area at which pro money pushed gbp. We have an overall price range of intelligent money to the tune of 900 points. The upper blue line is support and resistance and also supply. It has never been demand.

The blue box is the nearest supply we have and currently we are in the zone for selling but its not happening yet. Look at the past four weeks, its nothing but a parabolic move and unsustainable. Pro money is pushing hard to their target and the top end of the box is the obvious one. If the current weekly candle now forming ends with a long tail we have more clarity of higher prices to come. Price will have to take a breather soon and allow profits and positions be adjusted. With such a strong move up we now want to see a healthy pull back and into strong support to prevent such a powerful move falling back too far when the reverse gear is hit for profits and the forth coming shake out, how deep that goes will be down to how much appetite there is for pain. Even some of the big boys wont hold on too long for the continuation move to begin again. I see a lot of profit below the first supply area and would trade it carefully as we get closer to the top of the box. If we push through and come to sit on top of the box, then we look for target number 2. There are a few more months to worry about that.

Daily chart next. The blue box is even more important now and just look at the price action as we punched into it. You have some serious money making this happen and the same response when price hit it, immediate reversal and take profit. The current daily candle will probably close as it looks in this chart, right into the last area of supply.....sellers. This is a warning signal given we are at supply, resistance and back into supply for a second time. Price below this has no major support on the daily time frame. This means there is little substance behind the move here. But only here, remeber we always look for reasons on other time frames too. The lower white line is major support and resistance and where pro money came in initially. For price to push more into this box and show strength we need support below it. So far this chart looks like exhaustion.

Last chart is the 4hr. Lower white line is our support and the two blue lines in the middle are near term support, this is ok for the 4hr but its not near enough for a daily move. We came close to pulling back into the upper blue line today, but we really need to come back down much deeper. I marked one possible area for price to hit. Where price is now on this pair I would not take it either way. We either see the bulls push it into orbit and watch it fall off, or we see it come off now back down into a sensible area and then we catch the last push up.

Incidentally, the lack of 4hr and daily support is ignored supply on the weekly, can you spot it? This has significance for a continuation move to the upper over all range. I doubt most here need be concerned, it will take the deepest pockets to trade that. Tied into this is dollar weakness and other factors which will make the bulls strong.

The lower time frame analysis is all yours when the active markets take over tomorrow.

blacky, a number of things you need to look at closer. After you have satisfied yourself to the longer term direction of the market be sure to check the next lower time frame is ending its period of correction. Price action will often show it drifting off with little interest and once it hits old supply or demand you then drop down through lower time frames to the one you feel most comfortable trading and have the capital to take the draw down.

ideally you want to see a deep push back to the origin of a move which sets up the bias for pro money entering on that time frame. This all hinges on the higher time frames all lining up with their counter trend moves ending. The pull backs seem to be whats taking you out. You can use a wider stop, or wait for a later entry rather than try and pick a bottom or top which few people can do in the real world. Look for price to come back to where you now think is a good place, it is better to miss the odd entry while learning. Perhaps rather than take trades for a few days, just mark on screen where you would have entered with your current method. Mark every entry you think looks good and also mark your take profit. See how many 1st, 2nd and 3rd entries work out best. In time you will find where your eye can immediately spot the wise entries and not the emotional ones.

It is easy to post a chart and say enter here, and here etc. it is much more difficult on a live chart. Your targets look reasonable as you have planned them out well. Try the method for marking trades and post back here next week and let me know how its working out. Dont waste real money doing this, all you need is to train your eye and have a little more patience.
